title: Welcome to BlackRock Corporate site
gist: A BlackRock Investment Institute 'Global insights' note (bylined Ben Powell and Lamiaa Chaabi) arguing that softening oil revenue and maxed-out Gulf bank balance sheets are forcing GCC states to pivot from oil-and-bank funding to market-based finance. It quantifies the shift — Saudi total funding volume roughly tripled since 2022, loan-to-deposit ratios above 100% in Saudi/Qatar/Kuwait, ~$50bn of foreign energy-infrastructure commitments — and estimates ~$10bn of passive equity inflows and ~$5bn of initial EMBI flows from index-inclusion catalysts. The house view is constructive: hard-currency sovereign/quasi-sovereign carry, private infrastructure and transition-linked assets, selectively.

insights.claim: Brent crude has fallen roughly 50% from its post-Covid peak of about USD 128 per barrel in early 2022, driven by easing demand growth and the gradual return of OPEC+ supply, and prices are expected to stay contained as voluntary cuts unwind through late 2025 with the group signalling a pause on further increases in early 2026.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: A structurally capped oil price is the forcing function behind Gulf issuance supply — expect sustained GCC sovereign and quasi-sovereign bond flow rather than a cyclical blip.
insights.quote: Brent crude has declined by about 50% from its post-Covid pandemic peak of roughly USD $128 per barrel in early 2022

insights.claim: The IEA projects a widening oil supply surplus in the coming year that could add further downward price pressure, while BlackRock's own BII Transition Scenario has global oil demand peaking in the 2030s.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Two independent framings point the same way: underwrite Gulf credit on reform execution and non-oil revenue, not on an oil price recovery.
insights.quote: The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects a widening supply surplus next year that could place additional downward pressure on prices

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have each posted only one fiscal surplus in the past decade, showing that the funding gap in the Gulf is a decade-long structural condition rather than a recent shock.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Persistent deficits imply a durable pipeline of sovereign issuance and asset monetization — a structural supply story for EM hard-currency debt buyers.
insights.quote: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have posted only one fiscal surplus in the past decade

insights.claim: Loan-to-deposit ratios in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait stood above 100% as of Q2 2025 across an analysis of 22 banks' financial reports, limiting banks' capacity for additional lending and pushing borrowers toward market-based funding.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: The bank channel is the binding constraint — the trade is in the disintermediation it forces: bond, sukuk and securitization issuance, plus private credit and infrastructure capital filling the gap.
insights.quote: Loans-to-deposit ratios in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait stood at above 100% as of Q2 2025 based on our analysis of financial reports of 22 banks.

insights.claim: Since 2022, Saudi Arabia's total funding volume has roughly tripled, with a growing share coming from non-sovereign channels such as state-asset monetization and equity issuance.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Tripling volume with a shifting mix means the fee pool and the deal flow are migrating from bank lending to capital markets — favors ECM/DCM intermediaries and secondary-market liquidity.
insights.quote: Since 2022, Saudi Arabia’s total funding volume has roughly tripled, with a growing share coming from non-sovereign channels
insights.locator: The result is a growing shift toward market-based finance

insights.claim: Securitizing residential mortgages and easing rules on foreign real-estate ownership in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait are framed as a mechanism for freeing up bank balance-sheet capacity, not merely as housing or property policy.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Watch mortgage securitization volumes and foreign-ownership rule changes as the leading indicator of when Gulf bank lending capacity — and local credit growth — reopens.
insights.quote: show how financial reforms are freeing up bank capacity and diversifying sources of capital
insights.locator: Additional financial reforms are expanding local funding channels

insights.claim: Saudi pension assets equal about 31% of GDP per a 2024 IMF Financial Sector Assessment Program report, and as these pools expand they can become natural anchors for local bond and sukuk markets, providing long-term funding and valuation stability.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: A growing captive domestic bid is the structural support for local-currency Gulf duration — track pension-asset growth as the tell for local market depth.
insights.quote: Pension assets in Saudi Arabia equal about 31% of GDP

insights.claim: Chile is offered as the precedent for what institutionalized savings can do: its pension assets rose from 22% of GDP in 1990 to 76% in 2020, transforming local liquidity.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete multi-decade template and a benchmark path — a 31%-of-GDP starting point implies years of compounding local-market bid if the Chilean trajectory repeats.
insights.quote: in Chile, pension assets rose from 22% of GDP in 1990 to 76% in 2020, World Bank data show, transforming local liquidity

insights.claim: Discussions to lift Saudi Arabia's foreign-ownership limit to 100% could trigger about USD 10 billion of passive equity inflows, according to estimates from UBS, EFG Hermes, HSBC and other major brokers.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: A datable, sizeable passive bid — front-running the foreign-ownership-limit decision is a discrete event trade in Saudi equities.
insights.quote: discussions to lift Saudi Arabia’s foreign-ownership limit to 100% could bring about USD $10 billion of passive inflows
insights.locator: Integration of local assets into global benchmarks

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia's addition to the JPMorgan EMBI watchlist could draw roughly USD 5 billion of initial flows ahead of a likely 2026 index inclusion.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Gives a specific 2026 date and flow size for positioning in Saudi hard-currency sovereigns before benchmark buyers are forced in.
insights.quote: Saudi Arabia’s addition to the JPMorgan EMBI watchlist could draw roughly USD $5 billion of initial flows ahead of a likely 2026 inclusion
insights.locator: In fixed income, Saudi Arabia’s addition

themes.theme: AI and energy infrastructure as an asset class

insights.claim: International investors have committed about USD 50 billion to energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and the UAE in recent years, with large foreign-investment partnerships establishing a recurring model for inflows through long-term concessions and asset monetization.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Concession-and-monetization deals are becoming a repeatable, scalable template — a durable pipeline for private infrastructure allocators rather than one-off transactions.
insights.quote: International investors have committed about USD $50 billion in Saudi Arabia and the UAE in recent years

insights.claim: OpenAI's Stargate complex in the UAE and the Google–Public Investment Fund cloud region in Saudi Arabia are cited as evidence that digital infrastructure is emerging as a distinct asset class in the Gulf, while the 2024 JinkoSolar joint venture in Saudi Arabia shows the low-carbon transition embedding local manufacturing and technology transfer.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: The Gulf is being underwritten as an AI/data-center and localized clean-tech manufacturing destination — creates exposure via digital infrastructure and transition-linked private assets, not just oil.
insights.quote: Major artificial intelligence (AI) projects like OpenAI’s Stargate complex in the UAE and Google and the Public Investment Fund’s cloud region in Saudi Arabia highlight the rise of digital infrastructure as an asset class.
insights.locator: The region’s alignment with mega forces

insights.claim: The house view is constructive on the Gulf, favoring hard-currency sovereign and quasi-sovereign bonds for quality carry supported by robust sovereign balance sheets, index-inclusion momentum and global demand for duration and yield diversification, alongside private infrastructure and transition-linked assets in a granular multi-asset approach.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete allocation blueprint: GCC hard-currency credit for carry plus private infra/transition assets for compounding, sized granularly rather than as a broad regional beta bet.
insights.quote: Hard-currency sovereign and quasi-sovereign bonds continue to offer quality carry, supported by robust sovereign balance sheets, index-inclusion momentum and sustained global demand for duration and yield diversification.

insights.claim: The bullish case is explicitly conditional: progress is uneven, and global rate volatility, policy-execution risks and varying market depth require selectivity, with sustained momentum depending on governments actually following through on announced reforms.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: The trade is reform-execution-dependent — monitor delivery on announced reforms and market depth per country rather than treating the GCC as one homogeneous allocation.
insights.quote: Global rate volatility, policy-execution risks and varying market depth require selectivity in the long-term.
